Glass prism — from upload to simulation

Actual input · expected input · actual output · expected output · error propagation

Trace: TRACE-PRISM-20261016-004-NATIVE-RETRY-20261017

Trace ID: `TRACE-PRISM-20261016-004-NATIVE-RETRY-20261017`. These documents use the existing live native Windows request from 2026-10-17. No models, detectors or solvers were rerun while writing them. No production fixes were made. Source reference: A triangular glass prism with A=60°, an incident ray, internal and emergent rays, face normals, and symbolic incidence/refraction/emergence/deviation angles. Known and unknown evidence: 60° is printed apex-angle evidence. Vertices and rays require source measurement. No numerical refractive index is printed. An assumed index must not be described as measured from this diagram. Expected geometry for this diagram: Preserve the triangle sides/base and distinguish incident/internal/emergent rays from body edges and normal lines. Use observed base evidence rather than averaging unrelated side-segment extents. Expected initial simulation: At t=0 the prism polygon and ray segments should be compared with the printed paths. If a physical model with assumed n disagrees with the schematic, expose that disagreement; do not claim the computed path is observed source geometry. Exact expected coordinates/masks are unavailable: EXPECTED ARTIFACT NOT AVAILABLE — NO GROUND TRUTH EXISTS. Expected behavior below is a contract or a qualitative source comparison, never a hand-drawn expected result.

Markdown document · Original forensic call index

How to use this document

Read stages 01–34 in order. Blue panels show recorded data; green panels show expected contracts and source-specific requirements. Full snapshots are expandable. Mutation output is distinguished from a None/undefined function return. Earlier startup/demo events are excluded. A structural pass does not certify visual registration.

“NOT EXECUTED” means the branch did not run. “Not separately captured” means an internal operation was reached but its own call arguments were not intercepted. No expected pixels or runtime outputs have been invented.

  2. HTTP request reaches /api/ingest
  3. Upload persistence and dimension decoding

  18. Enforce authoritative source dimensions

  20. Resolution decisions, units and calibration
  21. Requirement and ambiguity analysis
  22. Readiness decision
  23. PhysicsCompiler entry and gate

  25. API response delivered to the browser

  27. Review / explicit compile request branch
  28. InteractiveFigure receives the compiled scene
  29. FigureViewport background and layout
  30. PhysicsRuntime normalization and adapter initialization
  31. Domain solver and actual initial state
  32. CoordinateMapper: source → overlay → browser
  33. Actual renderer at t=0 over the original
  34. Activation, motion and reset

What changed and what may have been lost

Expected output

Invertible mapping with the same image/overlay scale and offsets. Applying viewToSource(sourceToView(p)) should recover the supplied point within floating-point precision.

For this diagram

60° is printed apex-angle evidence. Vertices and rays require source measurement. No numerical refractive index is printed. An assumed index must not be described as measured from this diagram.

What changed and what may have been lost

sourceToView includes viewport letterboxing; sourceToOverlay omits it because the overlay is already image-aligned. Browser coordinates add the measured image origin. Do not add letterboxing twice.

Complete handoff JSON

Runtime subcomponents and capture boundary

These internal components are distinguished explicitly so a saved outer runtime result is not mistaken for six separate function traces.

ComponentExpected inputExpected outputActual evidence / gap
validatePhysicsSceneNormalized canonical sceneValidation result / typed issuesNot separately intercepted; successful load shows continuation, not a saved validation-result object.
SimulationCapabilityRegistry.resolveValidated normalized sceneInteractive scene/capabilitiesNo separate before/after capture. Use PhysicsRuntime source and actual runtime boundary; do not assume its output equals its input.
SolverRegistry.resolveInteractive sceneMatching domain adapterNo separately serialized adapter return. Runtime domain/output and the executed load path establish the adapter route.
Adapter.initializeInteractive scene, container and optionsInitialized adapter stateInitial runtime output/state is captured, but this child call’s exact argument object is not separately recorded.
Domain solverAdapter-derived model argumentsPhysics solution/stateActual solution/state is captured. Exact internal solver-call arguments are not a separate artifact.
Renderer.render / PendulumSimulation.renderRuntime solution/state and mapperSVG/canvas outputActual SVG/canvas and DOM measurements are captured; per-draw-call arguments are not.

Appendix B. First failure and propagation

Last known good: Exact source, correct prism semantics and OCR A=60°. Raw edges before OCR suppression retain the source boundaries.

First suspicious: The axis-aligned A=60° OCR box (556,184,128,49) and its four-pixel expansion intersect the slanted prism boundary. Later contour detection yields best_area=0; rays also includes body edges and normals.

First definitive failure: OCR edge masking erases prism-side pixels around A=60°; CV then infers an incorrect base from sloped-segment extents.

Downstream chain: Grounder preserves polygon and incident ray, records OCR apex angle=60°, but does not ground internal/emergent ray entities. Raw detected ray segments remain in evidence, not constraints for the runtime solution. A refractive index of 1.52 is auto-policy glass, not printed evidence. Existing incident origin/direction are retained; this run did NOT use a default horizontal incident ray. Compiler preserves CV vertices and incident input. Runtime recomputes refraction using n=1.52: hit1=(447.8163870862532,380.0386653684882), hit2=(807.0350434576367,409.11605562391077). The computed internal/emergent rays disagree visibly with the source. This is model re-synthesis from assumptions and incomplete observed ray constraints, not a proven Snell-law implementation error.

Separation of failure classes: preprocessing/perception is demonstrated upstream; a shared coordinate conversion error is not demonstrated; numerical solver failure is not established. The circuit never reaches a solver.

Appendix C. Capture limits

No new run was performed. The recorder captured repository Python boundaries and GenAI model calls, not private neural-library/C internals. JS boundary events, normalized scenes, actual solver outputs and DOM captures exist; separate entry/exit snapshots for every registry/adapter/renderer child function do not. These gaps are labeled, not filled with reconstructed output. Several void JS returns appear as captureError because undefined is not JSON; resulting state is separately recorded. Two class-serialization errors exist in the historical recorder log; integrity verification found the required snapshot files present for every indexed call. No exact expected pixel dataset, mask or numerical physical state has been authored.
